title: Souvenirs at the Office
titleJp: 職場[しょくば]のお土産[みやげ]

sentences.jp: 日本[にほん]で働[はたら]き始[はじ]めると、休[やす]みの後[あと]に同僚[どうりょう]がお菓子[かし]を配[くば]っているのを見[み]ることがあるでしょう。
sentences.en: Once you start working in Japan, you'll probably see coworkers handing out sweets after a holiday.

sentences.jp: これは「お土産[みやげ]」と呼[よ]ばれる習慣[しゅうかん]です。
sentences.en: This is a custom called omiyage.

sentences.jp: 旅行[りょこう]や帰省[きせい]で会社[かいしゃ]を休[やす]んだ人[ひと]は、その土地[とち]のお菓子[かし]などを買[か]ってきて、職場[しょくば]の人[ひと]に配[くば]ります。
sentences.en: People who took time off for a trip or a visit to their hometown buy sweets or other things from that area and hand them out to the people at work.

sentences.jp: お土産[みやげ]を配[くば]るのは、「休[やす]んでいる間[あいだ]、仕事[しごと]を代[か]わってくれてありがとう」という気持[きも]ちを伝[つた]えるためです。
sentences.en: The reason for handing out omiyage is to express the feeling of "Thank you for covering my work while I was away."

sentences.jp: そのため、高[たか]い物[もの]である必要[ひつよう]はありません。
sentences.en: For that reason, it doesn't need to be anything expensive.

sentences.jp: 大切[たいせつ]なのは、みんなに配[くば]りやすいことです。
sentences.en: What matters is that it's easy to share with everyone.

sentences.jp: 例[たと]えば、一[ひと]つずつ袋[ふくろ]に入[はい]っているクッキーやおせんべいなどがよく選[えら]ばれます。
sentences.en: For example, individually wrapped cookies or rice crackers are popular choices.

sentences.jp: 人数[にんずう]より少[すこ]し多[おお]めに買[か]っておくと、足[た]りなくなる心配[しんぱい]がありません。
sentences.en: If you buy a few more than the number of people, you won't have to worry about running out.

sentences.jp: 空港[くうこう]や駅[えき]には、その地方[ちほう]でしか買[か]えないお菓子[かし]がたくさん売[う]られています。
sentences.en: Airports and stations sell lots of sweets that you can only buy in that region.

sentences.jp: 渡[わた]すときは、「少[すこ]しですが、皆[みな]さんでどうぞ」などと一言[ひとこと]言[い]うといいでしょう。
sentences.en: When you hand them out, it's good to add a few words, such as "It's just a little something, but please help yourselves."

sentences.jp: 最近[さいきん]は、お土産[みやげ]をやめる職場[しょくば]も少[すこ]しずつ増[ふ]えているようです。
sentences.en: These days, it seems the number of workplaces that have stopped doing omiyage is gradually increasing.

sentences.jp: 迷[まよ]ったときは、まず周[まわ]りの人[ひと]がどうしているか、よく見[み]てみるのが一番[いちばん]です。
sentences.en: When you're not sure, the best thing is to first watch carefully what the people around you do.

sentences.jp: 海外[かいがい]から来[き]た人[ひと]なら、自分[じぶん]の国[くに]のお菓子[かし]を持[も]っていくと、話[はなし]のきっかけにもなって喜[よろこ]ばれるはずです。
sentences.en: If you're from overseas, bringing sweets from your own country will likely be appreciated, and it can also be a good conversation starter.

questions.q: What is the main feeling behind giving omiyage at work?
choices: Thanks to coworkers for covering your work while you were away
Following an order from the boss

questions.q: What kind of omiyage does the passage recommend?
choices: One large cake for the whole office
Individually wrapped snacks that are easy to share

questions.q: What advice does the passage give if you're unsure what to do?
choices: Watch what the people around you do
